city.Belize.description: Belize sits on the Caribbean coast of Central America. It is known for a giant round ocean sinkhole called the Great Blue Hole, a huge barrier reef, ancient Maya cities in the jungle, and the world's first jaguar reserve.
city.Belize.greeting: People here speak English, so just say hello with a friendly "Hello!"
city.Belize.flag: traced a flag: deep blue with a red stripe top and bottom and two woodcutters in a white circle
city.Belize.clue.0: studied a map of a small country tucked on the Caribbean coast of Central America
city.Belize.clue.1: wanted to dive into a giant, near-perfect round sinkhole in the middle of the sea
city.Belize.clue.2: tucked away a purse of leftover Belize dollars for the trip
city.Colombia.description: Colombia is a large country in northern South America touching both the Pacific and the Caribbean. It has snowy Andes peaks, thick Amazon rainforest, more kinds of birds than any other country, and a river that turns bright red.
city.Colombia.landmark: colorful flower-draped balconies of Cartagena's old walled city
city.Colombia.flag: a wide yellow band on top with blue and red below it
city.Colombia.clue.0: mapped out a big country at the very top of South America, touching two oceans
city.Colombia.clue.1: pointed at a guidebook page picturing Colombian peso notes
city.Costa Rica.description: This small, green country in Central America is famous for lush rainforests, misty cloud forests, and rumbling volcanoes. Bursting with wildlife, it gave up its whole army long ago to spend more on schools.
city.Costa Rica.landmark: perfect cone of Arenal Volcano behind lush rainforest with a bright toucan on a branch
city.Costa Rica.greeting: Most people speak Spanish — say hello with “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Costa Rica.flag: eyed a flag in a guidebook: blue and white stripes with a wide red band across the middle
city.Costa Rica.clue.0: packed for a small, green land of rainforests and rumbling volcanoes in Central America
city.Costa Rica.clue.1: loved that this peaceful place got rid of its entire army long ago
city.Cuba.description: This is the largest island in the whole Caribbean, known for lovingly kept 1950s cars rolling through Havana, hand-rolled cigars, and lively salsa and son music drifting from its sunny streets.
city.Cuba.landmark: bright vintage 1950s convertible driving past pastel colonial buildings in Old Havana
city.Cuba.greeting: Most people speak Spanish — say hello with “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Cuba.flag: drew a flag with blue and white stripes and a single white star in a red triangle
city.Cuba.clue.0: chattered about the biggest island in the whole Caribbean Sea
city.Cuba.clue.1: was thrilled to cruise past old buildings in a shiny 1950s American car
city.Cuba.clue.2: kept humming salsa tunes and bragging about famous hand-rolled cigars
city.Dominica.description: This tiny, mountainous island in the eastern Caribbean is nicknamed the “Nature Island” for its wild rainforests, hundreds of rushing rivers, a steaming boiling lake, and whales that swim offshore all year.
city.Dominica.greeting: The official language is English, but many people also greet you in Kwéyòl (a French Creole) with “Bonjou” (bon-ZHOO).
city.Dominica.flag: doodled a green flag with a cross of yellow, black, and white and a purple-and-green parrot in a red circle at the center
